 Luka Doncic breaks all-time NBA record, passes Michael Jordan with historic start 
 2026-11-05 06:50 
 Luka Doncic became the first player in NBA history with six straight games with at least 35 points, five rebounds, five assists, and five three-pointers, as the Lakers beat the Kings 116-103. His 38.5 points per game through eight appearances also moved him past Michael Jordan, with only Wilt Chamberlain having better starts to a season.

 Doncic finished with 40 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists as the Lakers defeated the Sacramento Kings 116-103 on Wednesday night, improving to 7-2 and extending their winning streak to three games.
 He knocked down six three-pointers and recorded his third consecutive 40-point performance.
 It was his sixth consecutive game with at least 35 points, five rebounds, five assists, and five made three-pointers, making him the first player in NBA history to produce such a streak, according to the Lakers.
 Doncic had matched Damian Lillard's previous record with his fifth straight such outing against the Miami Heat earlier in the week. Against Sacramento, he took the record for himself.
 Over the past six games, Doncic is averaging 42.8 points, 8.5 rebounds, and 8.3 assists, while shooting 52% from the field and 45% from three-point range.
 His latest 40-point night was already his fifth of the young season.
 Doncic joins Wilt, passes Jordan
 Doncic's historic start also ranks among the greatest scoring stretches to begin an NBA season.
 After scoring 268 points through his first seven appearances, Doncic added 40 against Sacramento to reach 308 points through eight games, an average of 38.5 points per game.
 Only Wilt Chamberlain has averaged more points through the first eight games of a season.
 Chamberlain averaged 52.3 points through eight games in 1962-63, 50.0 in 1961-62, and 39.6 in 1959-60. Doncic's 38.5 moves him just ahead of Michael Jordan's 38.4-point start in 1986-87.
 Milestone night in Lakers career
 Wednesday also marked Doncic's 100th game as a Laker.
 Across those first 100 appearances for Los Angeles, the Slovenian superstar has averaged 32.4 points, 7.9 rebounds, and 8.1 assists.
 Los Angeles will now return home to face the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday.
